subject: economics

concepts.title: Marginal Utility from Total Utility
concepts.definition: The additional amount of satisfaction an individual obtains from consuming one extra unit of a given commodity.
concepts.key_idea: Marginal utility equals the difference between current total satisfaction and prior total satisfaction.
question_patterns: calculate the marginal utility of the nth unit consumed
find the marginal utility when total utility changes from ... to ...
determine the addition to total utility from an extra unit
what is the marginal utility of the 5th unit
how much marginal utility is gained from the next item

solution_steps.action: subtract total utility of previous consumption level from current total utility
solution_steps.explain: Marginal utility is obtained by finding the increment in total utility from the additional unit

concepts.title: Marginal Rate of Substitution
concepts.definition: The quantity of one commodity a buyer must surrender to acquire an additional unit of another commodity while keeping aggregate welfare unchanged.
concepts.key_idea: Measures the trade-off between two commodities along a single indifference curve.
question_patterns: determine the marginal rate of substitution between two goods
what is the rate at which the consumer substitutes one good for another
calculate the MRS from the given bundle adjustments
find how many units of good 2 are foregone per extra unit of good 1
explain why the marginal rate of substitution declines along an indifference curve

solution_steps.action: identify the change in the sacrificed good and the acquired good
solution_steps.explain: Let delta_y be the reduction in good 2 and delta_x be the gain in good 1 along the indifference curve

solution_steps.action: evaluate the absolute ratio of change in good 2 to change in good 1
solution_steps.explain: MRS is the absolute magnitude of delta_y divided by delta_x

concepts.title: Properties of Indifference Curves and Monotonicity
concepts.definition: Key geometric traits characterizing consumer preferences including downward slope, convexity toward the origin, non-intersection, and higher curves reflecting greater welfare.
concepts.formula: IC slope < 0, convex to origin, IC_1 does not intersect IC_2
concepts.key_idea: Rational monotonic choice guarantees indifference curves slope downward, cannot intersect, and higher curves provide superior utility.
question_patterns: explain why two indifference curves can never intersect
verify whether the consumer preferences are monotonic across two bundles
why does an indifference curve slope downwards from left to right
what accounts for the convex shape of an indifference curve to the origin
show why a bundle with more of at least one good is strictly preferred

solution_steps.action: check bundle quantities across commodities
solution_steps.explain: Under monotonic preferences, a bundle having at least as much of all goods and more of one good is preferred

solution_steps.action: apply consistency condition to indifference curves
solution_steps.explain: Intersections lead to logical contradictions where two bundles have equal utility while one contains strictly more goods

concepts.title: Consumer Budget Constraint and Outlay
concepts.definition: The financial condition specifying that aggregate expenditure on all selected commodities cannot surpass available consumer income.
concepts.key_idea: The consumer can only afford bundles whose combined cost remains within total monetary income.
question_patterns: calculate the total expenditure of purchasing bundle x1 and x2
find whether a given consumption bundle is affordable within income
what is the total money spent on two goods at specified prices
determine the income required to purchase given quantities of both commodities
how much does a combination of two goods cost given their market prices

solution_steps.action: calculate expenditure on good 1
solution_steps.explain: Multiply unit price of good 1 by the quantity of good 1

solution_steps.action: calculate expenditure on good 2
solution_steps.explain: Multiply unit price of good 2 by the quantity of good 2

solution_steps.action: sum the expenditures on both goods
solution_steps.explain: Combine outlays on both commodities to find aggregate expenditure

concepts.title: Budget Line Intercepts and Shifts
concepts.definition: The boundary line representing all combinations whose total cost equals consumer income, characterized by intercepts on both axes and negative price-ratio slope.
concepts.key_idea: Income changes generate parallel shifts of the line whereas price variations pivot the line around an axis intercept.
question_patterns: write down the equation of the budget line
determine how the budget line shifts when consumer income increases
what happens to the budget line when the price of one good decreases
find the slope and intercepts of the budget line
explain the impact of a doubling of both prices and income on the budget set

solution_steps.action: formulate the budget line equation
solution_steps.explain: Set price_1 * x_1 + price_2 * x_2 equal to income M

solution_steps.action: evaluate intercepts and slope
solution_steps.explain: Horizontal intercept is M / price_1, vertical intercept is M / price_2, and slope is -price_1 / price_2

solution_steps.action: determine shift or pivot under parameter adjustments
solution_steps.explain: Proportional price and income changes leave the line unchanged; isolated income changes cause parallel shifts

concepts.title: Optimal Choice of the Consumer
concepts.definition: The condition under which a consumer attains the highest achievable indifference curve subject to the budget constraint.
concepts.key_idea: Consumer equilibrium is reached where the budget line is tangent to an indifference curve.
question_patterns: explain the condition for consumer equilibrium using indifference curves
why must MRS equal the price ratio at the optimum point
what happens if MRS is greater than the price ratio
determine why points below the budget line cannot represent consumer optimum
identify the optimal bundle on a diagram representing budget line and indifference curves

solution_steps.action: state the tangency condition between budget line and indifference curve
solution_steps.explain: Equilibrium occurs where the slope of the indifference curve equals the slope of the budget line

solution_steps.action: verify affordability and monotonicity requirements
solution_steps.explain: The optimal bundle must lie on the budget line as higher bundles are unaffordable and lower ones yield less satisfaction

concepts.title: Linear Demand Function Evaluation
concepts.definition: An algebraic relationship specifying the amount of a good demanded at any given unit price along a downward-sloping linear schedule.
concepts.key_idea: Quantity demanded declines linearly as price increases according to the slope factor.
question_patterns: calculate quantity demanded at a given price using a linear demand equation
find the demand for a good when price is ... and equation is q = a - bp
determine the consumer demand at the specified price level
what is the quantity demanded when price equals ...
how much of a good will be bought at price p under linear demand

solution_steps.action: calculate the price reduction component
solution_steps.explain: Multiply the slope parameter b by the market price

solution_steps.action: subtract price effect from autonomous demand
solution_steps.explain: Deduct price_effect from intercept_a to obtain quantity demanded

concepts.title: Determinants of Demand and Shifts in Demand Curve
concepts.definition: The effects on quantity demanded caused by changes in income, prices of substitutes or complements, and consumer tastes, differentiating shifts from movements along the curve.
concepts.key_idea: A change in own price leads to movement along the curve, while shifts in other factors displace the entire demand curve.
question_patterns: distinguish between movement along a demand curve and shift of the demand curve
how does an increase in the price of a substitute good affect demand
what happens to the demand curve for an inferior good when consumer income increases
explain the impact of a rise in complementary good price on demand
determine whether the demand curve shifts rightward or leftward

solution_steps.action: classify the changing determinant
solution_steps.explain: Identify whether the factor is own price, income, price of related goods, or consumer taste

solution_steps.action: determine the geometric response of the demand curve
solution_steps.explain: Own-price changes cause movement along the curve; changes in other variables cause parallel shifts

concepts.title: Market Demand Determination
concepts.definition: The total volume of a product demanded by all purchasers in a market across alternative price levels, derived by horizontal aggregation of individual demand schedules.
concepts.key_idea: Market demand is obtained by horizontally summing individual consumer quantities demanded at each price.
question_patterns: derive the market demand function from individual demand equations
calculate the market demand at each price from a given schedule of consumers
find the aggregate market demand for identical buyers
what is the horizontal summation of individual demand curves
how is the market demand curve derived graphically

solution_steps.action: specify individual demand curves for valid price domains
solution_steps.explain: Identify the non-negative demand region for each individual buyer

solution_steps.action: sum the quantities horizontally across all consumers at each price
solution_steps.explain: Add individual demand quantities together piecewise to form total market demand

concepts.title: Price Elasticity of Demand by Proportionate Method
concepts.definition: A quantitative measure of the degree of responsiveness of quantity demanded of a commodity with respect to a fractional variation in its price.
concepts.key_idea: Price elasticity equals the absolute ratio of percentage change in quantity to percentage change in price.
question_patterns: calculate the price elasticity of demand when price changes from ... to ...
find the price elasticity of demand using the proportionate method
what is the elasticity of demand if a price rise causes quantity to fall
compute the coefficient of price elasticity of demand
determine whether the demand for a good is elastic or inelastic

solution_steps.action: calculate absolute change in quantity
solution_steps.explain: Find the positive difference between initial quantity and new quantity

solution_steps.action: calculate absolute change in price
solution_steps.explain: Find the positive difference between initial price and new price

solution_steps.action: compute numerator as product of quantity change and initial price
solution_steps.explain: Multiply delta_q by price_1

solution_steps.action: compute denominator as product of price change and initial quantity
solution_steps.explain: Multiply delta_p by quantity_1

solution_steps.action: divide numerator by denominator to obtain elasticity
solution_steps.explain: Elasticity coefficient is num divided by den

concepts.title: Elasticity and Total Expenditure Relationship
concepts.definition: The qualitative framework analyzing the direction of change in total consumer expenditure resulting from price adjustments under different elasticity conditions.
concepts.key_idea: Expenditure moves opposite to price when demand is elastic, in the same direction when inelastic, and remains unchanged when unitary elastic.
question_patterns: explain how total expenditure changes when price rises and demand is inelastic
what happens to consumer spending when price drops and demand is elastic
determine the elasticity of demand if expenditure remains constant following a price change
how will total outlay be affected by an increase in commodity price
classify price elasticity based on the direction of change in expenditure

solution_steps.action: identify the direction of price movement and elasticity status
solution_steps.explain: Observe whether price increases or decreases, and whether elasticity is greater than, less than, or equal to one

solution_steps.action: deduce the response of total expenditure
solution_steps.explain: If elastic, expenditure moves opposite to price; if inelastic, expenditure moves with price; if unitary, expenditure is constant

questions: What do you mean by the budget set of a consumer?
What is budget line?
Explain why the budget line is downward sloping.

A consumer wants to consume two goods. The prices of the two goods are Rs 4 and Rs 5 respectively. The consumer's income is Rs 20. (i) Write down the equation of the budget line. (ii) How much of good 1 can the consumer consume if she spends her entire income on that good? (iii) How much of good 2 can she consume if she spends her entire income on that good? (iv) What is the slope of the budget line?
How does the budget line change if the consumer's income increases to Rs 40 but the prices remain unchanged?
How does the budget line change if the price of good 2 decreases by a rupee but the price of good 1 and the consumer's income remain unchanged?
What happens to the budget set if both the prices as well as the income double?

Suppose a consumer can afford to buy 6 units of good 1 and 8 units of good 2 if she spends her entire income. The prices of the two goods are Rs 6 and Rs 8 respectively. How much is the consumer's income?

Suppose a consumer wants to consume two goods which are available only in integer units. The two goods are equally priced at Rs 10 and the consumer's income is Rs 40. (i) Write down all the bundles that are available to the consumer. (ii) Among the bundles that are available to the consumer, identify those which cost her exactly Rs 40.
What do you mean by monotonic preferences?
If a consumer has monotonic preferences, can she be indifferent between the bundles (10, 8) and (8, 6)?
Suppose a consumer's preferences are monotonic. What can you say about her preference ranking over the bundles (10, 10), (10, 9) and (9, 9)?
Suppose your friend is indifferent to the bundles (5, 6) and (6, 6). Are the preferences of your friend monotonic?
Suppose there are two consumers in the market for a good and their demand functions are d1(p) = 20 - p for p <= 20, and d2(p) = 30 - 2p for p <= 15. Find out the market demand function.
Suppose there are 20 consumers for a good and they have identical demand functions d(p) = 10 - 3p for p <= 10/3, and d(p) = 0 for p > 10/3. What is the market demand function?
Consider a market where there are just two consumers and suppose their demands for the good are given in tabular form. Calculate the market demand for the good.
What do you mean by a normal good?
What do you mean by an inferior good? Give some examples.
What do you mean by substitutes? Give examples of two goods which are substitutes of each other.
What do you mean by complements? Give examples of two goods which are complements of each other.
Explain price elasticity of demand.

Consider the demand for a good. At price Rs 4, the demand for the good is 25 units. Suppose price of the good increases to Rs 5, and as a result, the demand for the good falls to 20 units. Calculate the price elasticity.
Consider the demand curve D(p) = 10 - 3p. What is the elasticity at price 5/3?
Suppose the price elasticity of demand for a good is -0.2. If there is a 5% increase in the price of the good, by what percentage will the demand for the good go down?
Suppose the price elasticity of demand for a good is -0.2. How will the expenditure on the good be affected if there is a 10% increase in the price of the good?
Suppose there was a 4% decrease in the price of a good, and as a result, the expenditure on the good increased by 2%. What can you say about the elasticity of demand?
